sanskrit: ye ca ke cana pārthānām abhiyātā dhanaṃjayam rājāno bhīṣmam āsādya gatās te yamasādanam
english: And whatever kings among the Pārthas advanced toward Dhanaṃjaya, once they came upon Bhīṣma they went to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: evaṃ daśa diśo bhīṣmaḥ śarajālaiḥ samantataḥ atītya senāṃ pārthānām avatasthe camūmukhe
english: Thus, having covered the ten directions on every side with nets of arrows, Bhīṣma broke through the army of the Pārthas and took his stand at the head of the host.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā sumahat karma tasmin vai daśame 'hani senayor antare tiṣṭhan pragṛhītaśarāsanaḥ
english: Having wrought that mighty deed on the tenth day, he stood between the two armies with his bow grasped firm.

sanskrit: na cainaṃ pārthivā rājañ śekuḥ ke cin nirīkṣitum madhyaṃ prāptaṃ yathā grīṣme tapantaṃ bhāskaraṃ divi
english: And none of the kings, O king, were able to gaze upon him, even as in the summer one cannot look upon the sun blazing at midheaven.

sanskrit: yathā daityacamūṃ śakras tāpayām āsa saṃyuge tathā bhīṣmaḥ pāṇḍaveyāṃs tāpayām āsa bhārata
english: As Śakra scorched the host of the Daityas in battle, so did Bhīṣma scorch the sons of Pāṇḍu, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tathā ca taṃ parākrāntam ālokya madhusūdanaḥ uvāca devakīputraḥ prīyamāṇo dhanaṃjayam
english: And beholding him so valorous, the slayer of Madhu, the son of Devakī, spoke with affection to Dhanaṃjaya:

sanskrit: eṣa śāṃtanavo bhīṣmaḥ senayor antare sthitaḥ nānihatya balād enaṃ vijayas te bhaviṣyati
english: "Yonder stands Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, between the two armies. Unless you slay him by force, victory shall not be yours.

sanskrit: yattaḥ saṃstambhayasvainaṃ yatraiṣā bhidyate camūḥ na hi bhīṣmaśarān anyaḥ soḍhum utsahate vibho
english: Be intent and hold him fast where this host is being shattered; for none other, O lord, has the strength to endure the arrows of Bhīṣma."

sanskrit: tatas tasmin kṣaṇe rājaṃś codito vānaradhvajaḥ sadhvajaṃ sarathaṃ sāśvaṃ bhīṣmam antardadhe śaraiḥ
english: Then in that instant, O king, he of the monkey-bannered standard, thus urged, hid Bhīṣma—with his standard, his chariot, and his horses—from sight beneath his arrows.

sanskrit: sa cāpi kurumukhyānām ṛṣabhaḥ pāṇḍaveritān śaravrātaiḥ śaravrātān bahudhā vidudhāva tān
english: But he too, the bull among the foremost of the Kurus, with showers of arrows scattered again and again the arrow-showers loosed by the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tena pāñcālarājaś ca dhṛṣṭaketuś ca vīryavān pāṇḍavo bhīmasenaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ
english: By him the king of the Pāñcālas, and valiant Dhṛṣṭaketu, and the Pāṇḍava Bhīmasena, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata,

sanskrit: yamau ca cekitānaś ca kekayāḥ pañca caiva ha sātyakiś ca mahārāja saubhadro 'tha ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: and the twins, and Cekitāna, and the five Kekayas as well, and Sātyaki, O great king, and the son of Subhadrā, and Ghaṭotkaca—

sanskrit: draupadeyāḥ śikhaṇḍī ca kuntibhojaś ca vīryavān suśarmā ca virāṭaś ca pāṇḍaveyā mahābalāḥ
english: the sons of Draupadī, and Śikhaṇḍin, and valiant Kuntibhoja, and Suśarman, and Virāṭa—those mighty warriors of the Pāṇḍava side—

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ pīḍitā bhīṣmasāyakaiḥ samuddhṛtāḥ phalgunena nimagnāḥ śokasāgare
english: these and many others, tormented by the shafts of Bhīṣma and sunk in an ocean of grief, were drawn forth and rescued by Phalguna.

sanskrit: tataḥ śikhaṇḍī vegena pragṛhya paramāyudham bhīṣmam evābhidudrāva rakṣyamāṇaḥ kirīṭinā
english: Then Śikhaṇḍin, swiftly seizing his supreme weapon, rushed straight at Bhīṣma, guarded by the diademed Arjuna.

sanskrit: tato 'syānucarān hatvā sarvān raṇavibhāgavit bhīṣmam evābhidudrāva bībhatsur aparājitaḥ
english: Then the unvanquished Bībhatsu, skilled in the orderings of battle, having slain all who followed in support, rushed straight at Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: sātyakiś cekitānaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ virāṭo drupadaś caiva mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau dudruvur bhīṣmam evājau rakṣitā dṛḍhadhanvanā
english: Sātyaki, and Cekitāna, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata, and Virāṭa, and Drupada, and the two sons of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas, charged at Bhīṣma in the fray, shielded by the steadfast bowman.

sanskrit: abhimanyuś ca samare draupadyāḥ pañca cātmajāḥ dudruvuḥ samare bhīṣmaṃ samudyatamahāyudhāḥ
english: And Abhimanyu in the battle, and the five sons of Draupadī, their great weapons raised aloft, charged at Bhīṣma in the fray.

sanskrit: te sarve dṛḍhadhanvānaḥ saṃyugeṣv apalāyinaḥ bahudhā bhīṣmam ānarchan mārgaṇaiḥ kṛtamārgaṇāḥ
english: All those firm-bowed warriors, never fleeing in battles, well practiced with their shafts, pierced Bhīṣma in many places with their arrows.

sanskrit: vidhūya tān bāṇagaṇān ye muktāḥ pārthivottamaiḥ pāṇḍavānām adīnātmā vyagāhata varūthinīm kṛtvā śaravighātaṃ ca krīḍann iva pitāmahaḥ
english: Shaking off those masses of arrows loosed by the foremost of kings, the grandsire, undaunted in spirit, plunged into the host of the Pāṇḍavas, warding off their shafts as though in sport.

sanskrit: nābhisaṃdhatta pāñcālyaṃ smayamāno muhur muhuḥ strītvaṃ tasyānusaṃsmṛtya bhīṣmo bāṇāñ śikhaṇḍinaḥ jaghāna drupadānīke rathān sapta mahārathaḥ
english: Smiling again and again and recalling the womanhood of the Pāñcāla prince, Bhīṣma did not aim at him; heedless of Śikhaṇḍin's arrows, the great warrior struck down seven chariots in Drupada's array.

sanskrit: tataḥ kilakilāśabdaḥ kṣaṇena samapadyata matsyapāñcālacedīnāṃ tam ekam abhidhāvatām
english: Then in an instant a tumultuous clamor arose from the Matsyas, the Pāñcālas, and the Cedis as they rushed upon him, the one man.

sanskrit: te varāśvarathavrātair vāraṇaiḥ sapadātibhiḥ tam ekaṃ chādayām āsur meghā iva divākaram bhīṣmaṃ bhāgīrathīputraṃ pratapantaṃ raṇe ripūn
english: With their throngs of fine horses and chariots, with elephants and footmen, they covered that one man—Bhīṣma, son of Gaṅgā, who was scorching his foes in battle—as clouds cover the sun.

sanskrit: tatas tasya ca teṣāṃ ca yuddhe devāsuropame kirīṭī bhīṣmam ānarchat puraskṛtya śikhaṇḍinam
english: Then, in that battle between him and them, a battle like that of gods and demons, the diademed Arjuna, putting Śikhaṇḍin to the fore, assailed Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evaṃ te paṇḍavāḥ sarve puraskṛtya śikhaṇḍinam vivyadhuḥ samare bhīṣmaṃ parivārya samantataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus all those Pāṇḍavas, putting Śikhaṇḍin to the fore, encircled Bhīṣma on every side and pierced him in the battle.

sanskrit: śataghnībhiḥ sughorābhiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ saparaśvadhaiḥ mudgarair musalaiḥ prāsaiḥ kṣepaṇībhiś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: With dreadful śataghnīs, with spiked maces and battle-axes, with hammers, clubs, and javelins, and with slings on every side,

sanskrit: śaraiḥ kanakapuṅkhaiś ca śaktitomarakampanaiḥ nārācair vatsadantaiś ca bhuśuṇḍībhiś ca bhārata atāḍayan raṇe bhīṣmaṃ sahitāḥ sarvasṛñjayāḥ
english: with gold-feathered arrows, with lances, pikes, and darts, with iron shafts, with calf-tooth barbs, and with bhuśuṇḍis, O Bhārata, all the Sṛñjayas together struck Bhīṣma in the battle.

sanskrit: sa viśīrṇatanutrāṇaḥ pīḍito bahubhis tadā vivyathe naiva gāṅgeyo bhidyamāneṣu marmasu
english: Then, his armor shattered and tormented by many, the son of Gaṅgā did not waver, though his vital parts were being pierced.

sanskrit: sa dīptaśaracāpārcir astraprasṛtamārutaḥ neminirhrādasaṃnādo mahāstrodayapāvakaḥ
english: With his blazing arrows and bow for flames, with the wind of his outpouring missiles, with the roar of his chariot-rims for thunder, and the rising of his great weapons for fire—

sanskrit: citracāpamahājvālo vīrakṣayamahendhanaḥ yugāntāgnisamo bhīṣmaḥ pareṣāṃ samapadyata
english: his wondrous bow a mighty blaze, the destruction of heroes its great fuel, Bhīṣma became to his foes like the fire at the end of an age.

sanskrit: nipatya rathasaṃghānām antareṇa viniḥsṛtaḥ dṛśyate sma narendrāṇāṃ punar madhyagataś caran
english: Plunging in and bursting out through the masses of chariots, he was seen again, ranging in the very midst of the kings.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāñcālarājaṃ ca dhṛṣṭaketum atītya ca pāṇḍavānīkinīmadhyam āsasāda sa vegitaḥ
english: Then, passing beyond the king of the Pāñcālas and Dhṛṣṭaketu, he swiftly reached the center of the Pāṇḍava host.

sanskrit: tataḥ sātyakibhīmau ca pāṇḍavaṃ ca dhanaṃjayam drupadaṃ ca virāṭaṃ ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pārṣatam
english: Then Sātyaki and Bhīma, and the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya, and Drupada and Virāṭa, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata—

sanskrit: bhīmaghoṣair mahāvegair vairivāraṇabhedibhiḥ ṣaḍ etān ṣaḍbhir ānarchad bhāskarapratimaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: these six he assailed with six arrows, terrible-sounding and swift, piercers of the foe's elephants, bright as the sun.

sanskrit: tasya te niśitān bāṇān saṃnivārya mahārathāḥ daśabhir daśabhir bhīṣmam ardayām āsur ojasā
english: But those great warriors, warding off his sharp arrows, tormented Bhīṣma with might, each with ten shafts.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu raṇe bāṇān yān mumoca mahāvrate te bhīṣmaṃ viviśus tūrṇaṃ svarṇapuṅkhāḥ śilāśitāḥ
english: And the arrows that Śikhaṇḍin loosed in the battle, O you of great vows—gold-feathered and whetted on stone—swiftly entered Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: tataḥ kirīṭī saṃrabdho bhīṣmam evābhyavartata śikhaṇḍinaṃ puraskṛtya dhanuś cāsya samācchinat
english: Then the diademed Arjuna, enraged, advanced straight upon Bhīṣma, and putting Śikhaṇḍin to the fore, cut his bow asunder.

sanskrit: bhīṣmasya dhanuṣaś chedaṃ nāmṛṣyanta mahārathāḥ droṇaś ca kṛtavarmā ca saindhavaś ca jayadrathaḥ
english: The great warriors did not brook the cutting of Bhīṣma's bow—Droṇa, and Kṛtavarman, and the lord of the Sindhus, Jayadratha,

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ śalaḥ śalyo bhagadattas tathaiva ca saptaite paramakruddhāḥ kirīṭinam abhidrutāḥ
english: Bhūriśravas, Śala, Śalya, and Bhagadatta as well: these seven, exceedingly wrathful, rushed upon the diademed one.

sanskrit: uttamāstrāṇi divyāni darśayanto mahārathāḥ abhipetur bhṛśaṃ kruddhāś chādayanta sma pāṇḍavān
english: Displaying their supreme celestial weapons, those great warriors, fiercely enraged, fell upon him and overwhelmed the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ śabdaḥ śuśruve phalgunaṃ prati udvṛttānāṃ yathā śabdaḥ samudrāṇāṃ yugakṣaye
english: The sound of them as they bore down upon Phalguna was heard like the roar of oceans surging up at the dissolution of an age.

sanskrit: hatānayata gṛhṇīta yudhyatāpi ca kṛntata ity āsīt tumulaḥ śabdaḥ phalgunasya rathaṃ prati
english: "Slay! Drive on! Seize! Fight! Cut him down!"—such was the tumultuous cry that arose against the chariot of Phalguna.

sanskrit: taṃ śabdaṃ tumulaṃ śrutvā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ abhyadhāvan parīpsantaḥ phalgunaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Hearing that tumultuous cry, the great warriors of the Pāṇḍavas ran forward seeking to protect Phalguna, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sātyakir bhīmasenaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ virāṭadrupadau cobhau rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: Sātyaki and Bhīmasena, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata, and Virāṭa and Drupada both, and the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca,

sanskrit: abhimanyuś ca saṃkruddhaḥ saptaite krodhamūrchitāḥ samabhyadhāvaṃs tvaritāś citrakārmukadhāriṇaḥ
english: and the wrathful Abhimanyu—these seven, swooning with rage, swiftly charged forward, bearing their gaily-painted bows.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ samabhavad yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam saṃgrāme bharataśreṣṭha devānāṃ dānavair iva
english: Between them arose a battle tumultuous and hair-raising, O best of the Bhāratas, like the conflict of the gods with the Dānavas.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu rathaśreṣṭho rakṣyamāṇaḥ kirīṭinā avidhyad daśabhir bhīṣmaṃ chinnadhanvānam āhave sārathiṃ daśabhiś cāsya dhvajaṃ caikena cicchide
english: But Śikhaṇḍin, foremost of charioteers, guarded by the diademed one, pierced Bhīṣma—his bow already cut—with ten arrows in the fray, and his charioteer with ten, and with one he severed his standard.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya gāṅgeyo vegavattaram tad apy asya śitair bhallais tribhiś ciccheda phalgunaḥ
english: The son of Gaṅgā took up another, swifter bow; but that too Phalguna cut to pieces with three sharp broad-headed shafts.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa pāṇḍavaḥ kruddha āttam āttaṃ punaḥ punaḥ dhanur bhīṣmasya ciccheda savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ
english: Thus the Pāṇḍava, enraged—Savyasācin, the scorcher of foes—cut asunder each bow of Bhīṣma's again and again as he took it up.

sanskrit: sa cchinnadhanvā saṃkruddhaḥ sṛkkiṇī parisaṃlihan śaktiṃ jagrāha saṃkruddho girīṇām api dāraṇīm tāṃ ca cikṣepa saṃkruddhaḥ phalgunasya rathaṃ prati
english: His bow cut through, and burning with wrath, licking the corners of his mouth, in his fury he seized a spear that could rend even mountains, and in his fury hurled it at the chariot of Phalguna.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ saṃprekṣya jvalantīm aśanīm iva samādatta śitān bhallān pañca pāṇḍavanandanaḥ
english: Seeing it bearing down, blazing like a thunderbolt, the joy of the Pāṇḍavas took up five sharp broad-headed arrows.

sanskrit: tasya ciccheda tāṃ śaktiṃ pañcadhā pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ saṃkruddho bharataśreṣṭha bhīṣmabāhubaleritām
english: In his wrath, O best of the Bhāratas, he cut that spear—hurled by the might of Bhīṣma's arm—into five pieces with his five shafts.

sanskrit: sā papāta paricchinnā saṃkruddhena kirīṭinā meghavṛndaparibhraṣṭā vicchinneva śatahradā
english: Cleft asunder by the wrathful diademed one, it fell like a lightning-flash broken loose and sundered from a bank of clouds.

sanskrit: chinnāṃ tāṃ śaktim ālokya bhīṣmaḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ acintayad raṇe vīro buddhyā parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Beholding that spear cut to pieces, Bhīṣma, filled with wrath—the hero, conqueror of hostile cities—reflected in his mind upon the battle:

sanskrit: śakto 'haṃ dhanuṣaikena nihantuṃ sarvapāṇḍavān yady eṣāṃ na bhaved goptā viṣvakseno mahābalaḥ
english: "I am able with a single bow to slay all the Pāṇḍavas, if only the mighty Viṣvaksena were not their protector.

sanskrit: kāraṇadvayam āsthāya nāhaṃ yotsyāmi pāṇḍavaiḥ avadhyatvāc ca pāṇḍūnāṃ strībhāvāc ca śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: For two reasons I shall not fight against the Pāṇḍavas: because the sons of Pāṇḍu are not to be slain, and because of the womanhood of Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: pitrā tuṣṭena me pūrvaṃ yadā kālīm udāvahat svacchandamaraṇaṃ dattam avadhyatvaṃ raṇe tathā tasmān mṛtyum ahaṃ manye prāptakālam ivātmanaḥ
english: Long ago, when he wedded Kālī, my father, well pleased, granted me death at my own will and invulnerability in battle. Therefore I deem this death to have come for me as if at its appointed hour."

sanskrit: evaṃ jñātvā vyavasitaṃ bhīṣmasyāmitatejasaḥ ṛṣayo vasavaś caiva viyatsthā bhīṣmam abruvan
english: Knowing thus the resolve of Bhīṣma of boundless splendor, the seers and the Vasus, standing in the sky, spoke to Bhīṣma:

sanskrit: yat te vyavasitaṃ vīra asmākaṃ sumahat priyam tat kuruṣva maheṣvāsa yuddhād buddhiṃ nivartaya
english: "What you have resolved, O hero, is to us a thing most dear. Do it, O mighty bowman; turn your mind away from battle."

sanskrit: tasya vākyasya nidhane prādurāsīc chivo 'nilaḥ anulomaḥ sugandhī ca pṛṣataiś ca samanvitaḥ
english: At the ending of that speech, an auspicious wind arose, favorable and fragrant, laden with droplets of water.

sanskrit: devadundubhayaś caiva saṃpraṇedur mahāsvanāḥ papāta puṣpavṛṣṭiś ca bhīṣmasyopari pārthiva
english: And the drums of the gods resounded with a mighty noise, and a rain of flowers fell upon Bhīṣma, O king.

sanskrit: na ca tac chuśruve kaś cit teṣāṃ saṃvadatāṃ nṛpa ṛte bhīṣmaṃ mahābāhuṃ māṃ cāpi munitejasā
english: And none, O king, heard those who spoke together, save mighty-armed Bhīṣma and myself, through the power of the sage.

sanskrit: saṃbhramaś ca mahān āsīt tridaśānāṃ viśāṃ pate patiṣyati rathād bhīṣme sarvalokapriye tadā
english: And a great agitation seized the gods, O lord of peoples, that Bhīṣma, beloved of all the worlds, was then about to fall from his chariot.

sanskrit: iti devagaṇānāṃ ca śrutvā vākyaṃ mahāmanāḥ tataḥ śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo bībhatsuṃ nābhyavartata bhidyamānaḥ śitair bāṇaiḥ sarvāvaraṇabhedibhiḥ
english: Having heard this speech of the hosts of gods, the great-souled Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, no longer advanced against Bībhatsu, though pierced by sharp arrows that cleft through every armor.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu mahārāja bharatānāṃ pitāmaham ājaghānorasi kruddho navabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But Śikhaṇḍin, O great king, in his wrath struck the grandsire of the Bhāratas in the chest with nine sharp arrows.

sanskrit: sa tenābhihataḥ saṃkhye bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ nākampata mahārāja kṣitikampe yathācalaḥ
english: Smitten by him in the battle, Bhīṣma, the grandsire of the Kurus, did not tremble, O great king, as a mountain trembles not in an earthquake.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya bībhatsur vyākṣipan gāṇḍivaṃ dhanuḥ gāṅgeyaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā kṣudrakāṇāṃ samarpayat
english: Then Bībhatsu, laughing, drew his bow Gāṇḍīva and pierced the son of Gaṅgā with twenty-five small arrows.

sanskrit: punaḥ śaraśatenainaṃ tvaramāṇo dhanaṃjayaḥ sarvagātreṣu saṃkruddhaḥ sarvamarmasv atāḍayat
english: Then again Dhanaṃjaya, hastening and full of wrath, struck him with a hundred arrows in all his limbs, in all his vital parts.

sanskrit: evam anyair api bhṛśaṃ vadhyamāno mahāraṇe na cakrus te rujaṃ tasya rukmapuṅkhāḥ śilāśitāḥ
english: Thus, though grievously struck by others as well in that great battle, those gold-feathered, stone-whetted shafts wrought him no pain.

sanskrit: tataḥ kirīṭī saṃrabdho bhīṣmam evābhyavartata śikhaṇḍinaṃ puraskṛtya dhanuś cāsya samācchinat
english: Then the diademed Arjuna, enraged, advanced straight upon Bhīṣma, and putting Śikhaṇḍin to the fore, cut his bow asunder.

sanskrit: athainaṃ daśabhir viddhvā dhvajam ekena cicchide sārathiṃ viśikhaiś cāsya daśabhiḥ samakampayat
english: Then, having pierced him with ten arrows, he severed his standard with one, and made his charioteer reel with ten shafts.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādatta gāṅgeyo balavattaram tad apy asya śitair bhallais tridhā tribhir upānudat nimeṣāntaramātreṇa āttam āttaṃ mahāraṇe
english: The son of Gaṅgā took up another, stronger bow; but that too, in less than the blink of an eye, he cut in three with three sharp broad-headed shafts, even as it was taken up, again and again, in that great battle.

sanskrit: evam asya dhanūṃṣy ājau ciccheda subahūny api tataḥ śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo bībhatsuṃ nābhyavartata
english: Thus he cut asunder very many of his bows in the fray; and thereafter Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, no longer advanced against Bībhatsu.

sanskrit: athainaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā kṣudrakāṇāṃ samardayat so 'tividdho maheṣvāso duḥśāsanam abhāṣata
english: Then he tormented him with twenty-five small arrows; and that mighty bowman, sorely pierced, spoke to Duḥśāsana:

sanskrit: eṣa pārtho raṇe kruddhaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathaḥ śarair anekasāhasrair mām evābhyasate raṇe
english: "Yonder Pārtha, the great warrior of the Pāṇḍavas, enraged in battle, presses upon me alone in the fray with arrows by the many thousands.

sanskrit: na caiṣa śakyaḥ samare jetuṃ vajrabhṛtā api na cāpi sahitā vīrā devadānavarākṣasāḥ māṃ caiva śaktā nirjetuṃ kim u martyāḥ sudurbalāḥ
english: He cannot be conquered in battle even by the wielder of the thunderbolt; nor are the heroes among gods, Dānavas, and rākṣasas, all together, able to vanquish me—how much less feeble mortals?"

sanskrit: evaṃ tayoḥ saṃvadatoḥ phalguno niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ śikhaṇḍinaṃ puraskṛtya bhīṣmaṃ vivyādha saṃyuge
english: While the two were thus speaking together, Phalguna, putting Śikhaṇḍin to the fore, pierced Bhīṣma in the fray with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tato duḥśāsanaṃ bhūyaḥ smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata atividdhaḥ śitair bāṇair bhṛśaṃ gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: Then, sorely pierced by the sharp arrows of the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, Bhīṣma, smiling, spoke once more to Duḥśāsana:

sanskrit: vajrāśanisamasparśāḥ śitāgrāḥ saṃpraveśitāḥ vimuktā avyavacchinnā neme bāṇāḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: "With a touch like the thunderbolt and the lightning, sharp-pointed, driven deep, loosed without break—these are not the arrows of Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: nikṛntamānā marmāṇi dṛḍhāvaraṇabhedinaḥ musalānīva me ghnanti neme bāṇāḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: Cutting through my vital parts, piercing my stout armor, they strike me like iron clubs—these are not the arrows of Śikhaṇḍin."
